The statement’s tone is mildly constructive: strong job gains and a low unemployment rate signal a tight labor market, while 12‑month inflation is near the symmetric 2% objective. In a Phillips-curve framework (unemployment related to inflation and expectations), such labor tightness would usually put upward pressure on prices, but the Fed notes market-based inflation compensation remains low and survey expectations are little changed—consistent with anchored expectations emphasized in sticky-information models (e.g., Mankiw–Reis) and with expected inflation influencing nominal rates via the Fisher channel. Viewing policy through a Taylor-rule/Taylor-principle lens, inflation near target and diminishing slack justify gradual rate increases toward neutral, aligning with the Committee’s guidance that the funds rate will remain below longer-run levels for some time. The decision to hold while signaling gradual hikes also reflects real-time data uncertainty highlighted by Orphanides, reinforcing a cautious, accommodative stance amid moderated household spending but strong business investment. Net assessment: positive on growth and employment, balanced on inflation risks.
